definitions.explanation: A polite or neutral way to refer to an adult male.

examples.english: A man asked me for directions at the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{背|せ}→背：02907_se⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧{男|おとこ}の{人|ひと}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}って→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦きた→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧{男|おとこ}の{人|ひと}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{走|はし}っている→走る：00519_hashiru⟧。
examples.english: That man runs in this park every morning.
A man gave up his seat for me on the train, so I thanked him.

notes:
{男|おとこ}の{人|ひと} is the standard polite way to refer to an adult male in everyday conversation. It is neutral and appropriate in most situations.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{男|おとこ}→男：00561_otoko⟧: man (more direct, slightly casual)
- ⟦{男性|だんせい}→男性：01655_dansei⟧: male (formal, used in official/medical/survey contexts)
- ⟦{紳士|しんし}→紳士：18022_shinshi⟧: gentleman (respectful, formal)
- ⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧: boy, male (used in school/sports contexts)
⟦{女|おんな}の{人|ひと}→女の人：noentry⟧ (woman) follows the same pattern.

USAGE:
Used when describing or referring to men you do not know personally. In casual speech, {男|おとこ}の{人|ひと} is more natural than ⟦{男性|だんせい}→男性：01655_dansei⟧, which sounds stiff. When talking about someone specific, a name or title is preferred.
